description: Smash the stack. Can you overflow the correct buffer? The program reads input with gets and a signal handler prints the flag on crash.
Control the return address. Overflow the buffer and return to the flag function in the program. Source uses gets into a small stack buffer.

description: Check the admin scratchpad. After login a cookie named jwt appears. Have you heard of JWT? The site blocks the username admin at the form but trusts the token role.

description: A menu-driven program allocates two heap buffers next to each other. Overflowing the input buffer overwrites a neighbouring safe variable used as a flag gate.
This website lets you read files after login. The read endpoint checks a MAC over the filename. Flag is at /etc/flag.txt. Hints mention cheese length and implementing MAC.

description: The ciphertext looks like English letters with shifted alphabet positions. Frequency analysis should recover the plaintext motto.

description: You are given a USB disk image. Recover a deleted document from unallocated space. Standard forensic imaging formats apply.

description: NX is enabled so shellcode will not run on the stack. There is a win function already in the binary. Overflow the buffer and return to it.

A stack canary protects against buffer overflows. Leak or brute the canary, then overwrite the return address.
Two heap chunks sit next to each other. Overflowing the first overwrites a neighbouring safe variable used as a gate.
The program prints user input with printf. Using format specifiers, leak addresses and overwrite a GOT entry.

The same message was encrypted under two RSA public keys that share a modulus. Recover the plaintext without factoring.
Two ECDSA signatures were produced with the same ephemeral nonce. Recover the private key from the pair of signatures.
